html:
On 12 March 1938 German troops marched into Austria, and the next day Austria was declared part of Nazi Germany. The union is called the Anschluss.

Many Austrians and Germans had wanted union since 1918, but the peace treaties forbade it. Hitler, himself Austrian born, pressed the chancellor Kurt Schuschnigg to give power to Austrian Nazis. When Schuschnigg called a referendum on independence, Hitler forced him out and invaded. Crowds cheered Hitler in Vienna, and a staged vote in April approved the union with over 99 percent.

At once Jews in Vienna were beaten, robbed and humiliated in the streets. Most of Austria's Jews fled or were later killed in the Holocaust. After the war Austria long described itself as Hitler's first victim, a view questioned since the 1980s. The State Treaty restored independence in 1955. See Austria.
sum: On 12 March 1938 German troops marched into Austria, and the next day Austria was declared part of Nazi Germany. The union is called the Anschluss.
